idiom_name: Slick table foreignKey(...) plus join navigators
implementation_notes: Slick declares the constraint on the table class: foreignKey("SUP_FK", supID, suppliers)(_.id, onUpdate = ForeignKeyAction.Restrict, onDelete = ForeignKeyAction.Cascade) makes the key and its actions first-class in DDL, and a plain query method (suppliers.filter(_.id === supID)) is the navigator that resolves it; mapped tables built with <> (User.tupled, User.unapply) connect rows to case classes. Doobie or plain JDBC remains the justified hand-written option when the SQL must be literal, in which case the foreign key is just a column you resolve yourself.
pitfalls: Nullable columns are Option[T] but predicates follow the database's null propagation (None === None yields None), so a NULL foreign key does not behave like Scala's Option.
Constraints are discovered reflectively as methods returning ForeignKeyQuery: dismissing the method silently removes the constraint from DDL while the join navigator keeps compiling.
Table classes are macros over tuples, so the * projection and the case class must stay in step or row mapping fails at runtime.
